$comment: Default jev-dispatch configuration. Copy to ~/.jev-dispatch/config.json (or .yaml) and edit. Every value here is overridable; user config is deep-merged over this.

semanticEvaluator.$comment: Who answers the policy graph's boolean predicates. The graph itself is unaffected by this choice. jev calls TypeSafe or a gateway; laya runs locally through the model authors' own package; mock returns fixed answers. Leaving this out keeps the original behaviour, which is jev. The laya settings - model, runtime, python, timeouts - default in src/router/engines/laya.mjs so there is one place to read them; add a laya block here to override them.

jev.$comment: provider picks the defaults below; every one of them can be overridden. Only the typesafe shape has been checked against a running service — run `jev-dispatch check-router` before trusting another.

low.description: Mechanical and local: the work is obvious, single-step, or pure lookup/formatting. Any fast small model does it just as well.

medium.description: Ordinary engineering: a few dependent steps using familiar patterns, little ambiguity, a competent mid-tier model is enough.

high.description: Hard or high-stakes: cross-cutting design, subtle debugging, interacting constraints, or correctness matters more than cost.

facts.$comment: Deterministic evidence gathered once before routing, never from inside a policy predicate. Off by default: with enabled false the dispatcher behaves exactly as it did before, and Semgrep is never invoked. semgrep.config is resolved relative to the task's working directory, so each repository carries its own rules. Targets are the files the caller named as relevant context, falling back to the whole working directory when it named none — a full-repo scan rarely fits a routing budget, and the named files are what the subtask is about. A rule says which logical fact it stands for through metadata.dispatcher.fact, which is the mechanism to prefer. ruleFacts is the fallback for rules you cannot annotate and wins over metadata, but it is keyed on Semgrep's check_id, which prefixes the rule id with the rules file's directory (.semgrep/dispatcher.yml gives semgrep.<id>) - a mapping written from the rule file alone never matches and never says so, so check it with 'jev-dispatch facts'. Policies name facts, never Semgrep rule ids.
